label: churn200-s9
summary: The model scores churn as the sigmoid of a sum of parts. Customer service calls matter most once a customer has made three or more calls: for a typical customer the predicted risk is 1.2% at two calls, 9.9% at four and 82.5% at six, and the rise is steeper for light daytime users. A high day charge raises risk steeply for customers without voicemail messages (typical customer: 1.2% at a thirty-dollar day charge, 78.1% at fifty dollars), and a high evening charge adds to it when the day charge is high, while lowering risk slightly when the day charge is low. An international plan raises a typical customer's risk from 1.2% to 17.5%. The voicemail plan, international charge and account length enter mainly as direct linear terms; the state units and two tail terms on the heaviest callers barely change the ranking. Training AUC is 0.914; switching off the charge parts, the service-call parts or the international plan part lowers it to 0.805, 0.810 and 0.862. Structural and compositional coverage are complete, and the annotated network reproduces the original on every training row to within 5.6e-16.

refuted_and_fixed: day_charge_no_voicemail: 'any voicemail message closes the gate' was refuted by the probe (a $60 day charge with 10 messages keeps it open); rewritten to 'each message pushes it shut' plus the training count of open-gate customers with messages
customer_service_terms: 'steeper for light daytime users' first quoted whole-model risks, which the charge parts confound; rewritten to the group's own contribution
total_charge_gate: first drafted as 'high charges raise risk'; the probe showed the evening charge lowers risk at a low day charge, so the hypothesis states the interaction
